gen_risks.description: Delay in recruiting required PIU specialists (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) within the one‑month deadline.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop an accelerated recruitment plan, use interim contracts, and set weekly hiring milestones monitored by the World Bank team.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, appoint... an accountant, a gender‑based violence consultant (Financing Agreement).

gen_risks.description: Failure to customize existing accounting software for project bookkeeping within three months.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage an IT vendor before effectiveness date, allocate dedicated budget, and conduct bi‑weekly progress reviews against a detailed work plan.
gen_risks.evidence: customize the existing accounting software... no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date (Financing Agreements for CEMAC, CAR, Cameroon).

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays caused by weak market competition and limited supplier capacity in fragile settings.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early market engagement, adopt flexible procurement methods, and provide capacity‑building for local suppliers to broaden competition.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings (Section IV.B).

gen_risks.description: High fiduciary risk – overall financial management (FM) residual risk rated Substantial for all implementing agencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement FM capacity upgrades, update FM manuals, recruit external auditors, and conduct quarterly internal audits with World Bank supervision.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall FM residual risk rating is assessed as Substantial... for CEMAC, Cameroon, CAR, Chad, and RoC (Section IV.B).

gen_risks.description: Environmental impacts from construction, laboratory waste and hazardous material handling.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare site‑specific ESMPs, follow the Umbrella ESF, train staff on waste segregation, and monitor compliance through regular audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential impacts include waste, dust, emission, occupational health and safety, and hazardous material disposal (Section D. Environmental and Social).

gen_risks.description: Sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH) risks linked to expanded community health workforce.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV and SEA/SH risk assessments, develop Action Plans, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, and train all staff on reporting protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Overall project SEA/SH risks are substantial; PIUs will prepare GBV and SEA/SH risk assessments and Action Plans (Section on SEA/SH).

gen_risks.description: Political instability and conflict in Cameroon, CAR and Chad disrupting service delivery and project activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement flexible implementation schedules, develop security risk assessments, maintain contingency funds, and coordinate closely with local authorities and UN agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: Political instability... may disrupt service delivery (Cameroon appraisal); ongoing conflict in CAR and Chad noted throughout the document.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related floods and extreme weather damaging health facilities and surveillance infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design all facility upgrades to climate‑resilient standards, incorporate flood‑risk mapping, and install solar‑powered backup systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Seasonal floods... raise disease risk; climate change contributes to 50% of natural disasters (Regional Context).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient domestic financing jeopardizing long‑term sustainability of health security investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support integration of health security into national budgets, develop Medium‑Term Expenditure Frameworks, and explore public‑private partnership pilots.
gen_risks.evidence: Securing financial sustainability... will be supported to integrate health security into national budgeting processes (Sustainability section).

gen_risks.description: Weak cross‑border coordination leading to delayed detection and response to outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC), formalize MoUs with neighboring states, and conduct regular joint simulation exercises.
gen_risks.evidence: Regional cross‑border collaboration is essential; RCC will meet regularly and support routine investigations/simulations (Section II.C).

gen_risks.description: High turnover or capacity gaps among PIU staff causing implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer retention incentives, implement continuous professional development, and maintain a pool of standby qualified personnel.
gen_risks.evidence: PIUs will be staffed with specialists; risk of questionable expenditures in remote areas noted (Cameroon FM assessment).

gen_risks.description: Delays in achieving laboratory accreditation (SLIPTA) reducing detection capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance, set phased accreditation milestones, and monitor progress through quarterly lab performance reports.
gen_risks.evidence: Participating Countries with project‑supported laboratories have achieved a 3‑star rating or higher during a SLIPTA audit (Indicators).

gen_risks.description: Gender gap in epidemiology and veterinary training limiting workforce effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement gender‑targeted recruitment, set minimum female participation quotas in training programs, and provide flexible learning formats.
gen_risks.evidence: Women remain underrepresented; project aims for at least 10% increase in female epidemiologists (Gender section).

gen_risks.description: Security threats to staff operating in conflict‑affected or IDP‑hosting areas.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement Security Risk Assessments and Security Management Plans, provide security training, and secure insurance for high‑risk travel.
gen_risks.evidence: PIUs will prepare a Security Risk Assessment (SRA) and Security Management Plan (SMP) (Section on Security).

gen_risks.description: Delays in finalizing the MoU between CEMAC and WOAH, affecting animal health coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set a firm deadline, assign a liaison officer, and monitor progress through monthly coordination meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient shall, no later than ninety (90) days after the Effective Date, enter into a MoU with WOAH (Financing Agreement).

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
